newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to hold local elections in June.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to hold local elections in June.

text.p: Morocco will hold local council elections on June 13, Interior Minister Driss Basri said on Monday.
He told a news conference in Casablanca that campaigning would start on May 29 and close on June 12.
Local councils will later elect representatives to about 80 percent of seats in a new upper house of parliament being set up under constitutional reforms agreed last September.
"The date of communal and municipal elections has been set for Friday, June 13, 1997," Basri told reporters.
Voting will be held throughout the country, including the disputed Western Sahara territory.
The June polls are the first of a series which will culminate in parliamentary elections in September. King Hassan will inaugurate a new bicameral parliament in October.
The lower house of parliament will be elected directly and the upper house indirectly. The upper house will have the power to vote out the government.
The existing 333-seat parliament is controlled by centre-right parties, with opposition parties holding 125 seats.
